models.sample_description: Annual industrial-firm observations for 1979–1998 drawn from Compustat 1999 PST and full-coverage files. The initial screen yielded 64,663 firm-year observations for 7,629 firms, requiring nonmissing current- and preceding-year SG&A and net sales and excluding firm-years where SG&A exceeded sales. The pooled one-year Model (I) fit excludes the top and bottom 0.5% of any model variable, leaving 63,958 observations.
models.method_details: The authors estimate Model (I) using ordinary least squares on the pooled sample.

estimation_procedure.description: Pooled estimation of the one-year change specification; current and preceding annual SG&A and net sales values form the ratios. This is the authors’ selected baseline before adding lagged revenue-change terms or aggregating changes over multiple years.

preprocessing.description: The initial data screen requires nonmissing current- and preceding-year SG&A costs and net sales revenue and deletes firm-years where SG&A costs exceed sales revenue.

evidence.quote: We screened the data for missing observations of either SG&A costs or sales revenue in the current or preceding year and deleted observations if SG&A costs exceeded sales revenue.

preprocessing.description: The authors exclude an observation if any model variable is in the top or bottom 0.5% of its distribution, reducing the 64,663 screened observations by 705 to 63,958.

evidence.quote: We eliminated extreme observations from the estimation by excluding an observation if the value of any variable was in the top or bottom 0.5% of its distribution (Chen and Dixon [1972]), resulting in a reduction of 705 observations to 63,958 observations.

other.description: The authors report that White’s test did not indicate a heteroskedasticity problem for the loglinear model. Their firm-by-firm Durbin–Watson test found positive autocorrelation for fewer than 3% of firms and led them to conclude serial-correlation correction was unnecessary.

evidence.quote: White’s [1980] test indicated that heteroskedasticity was not a problem for our loglinear model.

The Durbin-Watson [1951] test statistic revealed significant (at the 5% level) positive autocorrelation for less than 3% of the firms, indicating that it was not necessary to correct for serial correlation in the data.

other.description: The authors selected the ratio/log specification over a linear specification after a Davidson–MacKinnon test rejected the linear form in favor of the loglinear model.

evidence.quote: Empirically, the Davidson and MacKinnon [1981] test rejects the linear form in favor of this loglinear model.

scope.quote: We test for sticky cost behavior by estimating an empirical model that relates changes in SG&A costs to contemporaneous changes in net sales revenue.
This model provides the basis for our test of stickiness of SG&A costs.
We present the results of estimating model (I) for the pooled sample in table 2.

method.quote: We estimated the model using ordinary least squares (OLS).

equation.quote: Model (I): <u>Revenuei,t</u> Revenuei,t −1 log <u>SG&Ai,t</u> SG&Ai,t −1 = β 0 + β 1 log + εi,t . + β 2 ∗ Decrease Dummyi,t ∗ log <u>Revenuei,t</u> Revenuei,t −1
This model provides the basis for our test of stickiness of SG&A costs.

sample.quote: The data set includes annual data for industrial firms covering the 20 years from 1979 to 1998.
Data were drawn for all firms included in the PST (primary, supplementary, and tertiary) and full-coverage files of Compustat 1999.
The total number of remaining observations is 64,663 for 7,629 firms, an average of about 8.5 observations per firm.

We eliminated extreme observations from the estimation by excluding an observation if the value of any variable was in the top or bottom 0.5% of its distribution (Chen and Dixon [1972]), resulting in a reduction of 705 observations to 63,958 observations.

review_notes: Source-first scope is the primary one-year pooled Model (I) test of contemporaneous SG&A cost stickiness. Model (II) adds lagged changes to test reversal; two-, three-, and four-year Model (I) columns test the separate period-aggregation hypothesis. Firm-specific time-series, alternative estimators, and later hypotheses are not part of this selected baseline family.
descriptive_reason: Table 1 reports raw annual revenue and SG&A levels and sign-conditioned raw decrease summaries related to the retained log-change variables. results_review_notes: Only the frozen pooled Model (I), one-year baseline column is extracted. Model (II), longer aggregation periods, a no-interaction comparison, later fixed-effects fits, and year-by-year coefficient summaries are outside the selected result set.

The Table 1 SG&A-to-revenue percentage is not included because it is a constructed ratio rather than a retained predictor or upstream input. Raw revenue and SG&A levels and negative-change summaries are retained as related source data.
